title: Recover constant-pool concat before porting a custom digest
invariant: When a named textbook digest or cipher misses a captured digest or key, prove prefix and suffix joins against recovered constant-pool or derived strings before rewriting IVs, round functions, or compress steps.

appliesWhen: a helper is named or fingerprinted as a textbook digest or block cipher
the unsalted caller, plaintext, or apparent key misses the captured digest or wire field
constant-pool, data-segment, or derived strings are available as concat or slice candidates
stopsWhen: the unsalted caller already matches the captured digest
prefix and suffix joins both miss after packing, encoding, and IV or round checks
the captured alphabet or length is a different primitive family
a host-object property read is observed entering the preimage

oracles.positive: python scripts/experience_fixture_check.py references/experience-fixtures/standard-primitive-concat-matrix.json reports positiveOracle=true, concatMatched=true, and unsaltedMissed=true
oracles.negative: setting unsalted-caller.digestMatchesCaptured=true or changing capturedDigest away from md5(caller+suffix) must fail the fixture checker

decision.action: freeze the captured digest, test unsalted then prefix and suffix joins against recovered constant-pool or derived strings, and keep the textbook primitive when a join hits
decision.fallback: if prefix and suffix joins both miss, open packing, encoding, IV, and round-function checks instead of inventing a new primitive name
